svg.title: The security-management decision cycle
svg.desc: Educational redraw, not an official process diagram. Law, contracts, policy, authorization, accountability and evidence handling apply throughout. Activities may overlap; improvement feeds risk assessment. Risk Management: Identify important assets and threats; assess likelihood, impact and existing controls; set priorities and review dates. Incident Response: Check alerts against original evidence. Contain harm, address causes and verify recovery within authorization; do not close a case on guesses. Continuous Improvement: Find detection and process gaps; update access, procedures, exercises and training. Return to risk management: Use lessons learned to reassess residual risk. Fixing one vulnerability does not manage every risk; closing an alert does not prove safety.
